title: Trustworthy Multimodal Edge Perception: A Survey of AI Model Integrity from Supply-Chain Provenance to Attested Deployment
abstract: Supplementary code and data for the survey "Trustworthy Multimodal Edge Perception: A Survey of AI Model Integrity from Supply-Chain Provenance to Attested Deployment" (C. Pakkam Isaac and S. Venkatanarayanan). This archive accompanies the paper and contains three components: (1) Per-reference tracker (tracker.csv) — the audit trail for the survey's 166-reference corpus, recording each reference's primary category, source type, and year. (2) Evidence-layer reference implementation (evidence_graph.py) — a small, self-contained tool that builds a tamper-evident "evidence graph" for a machine-learning model supply chain and measures the cost of the cryptographic evidence layer (SHA-256 hashing, Ed25519 signing and verification, attestation-quote construction, full-chain verification, traceability queries, and tamper detection). Captured results are included for two platforms: a commodity x86-64 host (results.json) and an Arm edge platform (results_jetson.json), along with an environment-capture script (capture_jetson_env.py) and a one-command runner (run_jetson.sh). (3) Illustrative backdoor-detection experiment (backdoor_experiment/) — code and results for a demonstration that where a control sits in the model lifecycle changes what it catches, comparing a build-time model scan (Neural Cleanse) against a runtime input screen (STRIP) on a pool of clean and backdoored CIFAR-10 classifiers. Each result file records the exact runtime environment for reproducibility. See README.md for structure and run instructions. License: code and results are released under the MIT License; the reference tracker (tracker.csv) is released under CC-BY-4.0. See the bundled LICENSE and README.md for details.

title: Voice and Speech Recognition Transforming Human and Machine Communication
abstract: According to MarkNtel Advisors, the global voice and speech recognition market value was approximately USD 15.78 billion in 2024 and is projected to reach around USD 36.08 billion by 2030, with an estimated CAGR of 14.78% during 2025–2030. The report identifies healthcare adoption as a prominent driver and notes that artificial intelligence-based solutions hold a significant share. AI systems learn from large speech datasets covering different languages, accents, speaking styles, and environments. This supports better transcription, intent detection, sentiment analysis, and speaker identification. Cloud platforms also allow organizations to add voice features without building every component internally. As enterprises automate routine interactions, speech technology is being integrated into customer service, analytics, security, documentation, and employee productivity tools.

title: Federated Learning in Smart Healthcare
abstract: Transformation of medical diagnostics, treatment & patient management is fundamental in the new era of smart healthcare, integration of advanced technologies and data analytics. The extensive use of large-scale medical data lays the heart of this medical transformation. This raises concerns regarding patient privacy & data security. There is a great risk of an increase in data breaches and unauthorised access as there is more use of traditional centralised machine learning models. Federated Learning (FL) has emerged as a revolutionary approach that enables decentralised machine learning to address the challenges. FL allows models to be trained across multiple devices or institutions without the need to centralise sensitive data. This chapter explores the applications and potential of FL within smart healthcare systems. Primarily highlighting patient data privacy, enhancing model accuracy and optimising healthcare delivery. This research intends to advance the field of medical data analysis while safeguarding patient privacy as FL is integrated into smart healthcare.

title: Efficient multi-body shape optimization of on-chip nanophotonic neural network
abstract: Inverse design of on-chip nanophotonic neural networks (ONNs) is often hindered by the prohibitive cost of repeated three-dimensional (3D) full-wave simulations, especially when the optimization is performed in a high-dimensional geometric design space. Here, we employ a computationally efficient multi-body shape optimization framework and integrate it with a wave-based linear-decoupling strategy to address this challenge. By reconstructing input-specific responses from pre-computed characteristic states, our approach bypasses the need for exhaustive, repetitive full-wave solutions of Maxwell’s equations inside the optimization loop. We utilize elliptical scatterers to enable anisotropic control over optical fields, reducing the nominal design-variable count by hundreds of times for the studied devices compared to an equivalent 40-nm pixel-based topology-optimization baseline. 3D finite-difference time-domain simulations on the Iris and MNIST classification benchmarks validate that the proposed framework yields compact ONN classifiers with high inference accuracy and significantly lower training cost. This work establishes a scalable, fabrication-aware methodology for high-performance on-chip photonic neural processors.

This work establishes a scalable, fabrication-aware methodology for high-performance on-chip photonic neural processors.

title: Enhancing out-of-hospital emergency care via lexical machine learning modeling of chief complaints
abstract: Emergency medical services (EMS) professionals make high-stakes decisions in austere environments. To support out-of-hospital emergency care, we developed an AI model that leverages lexical data to predict receipt of lifesaving intervention (LSI) in the field. Using a large, nationwide EMS data set, we extracted free-text, clinician-generated chief complaints and receipt of out-of-hospital LSI from the electronic health record. In our derivation cohort (CY2023; n = 9,171,818), we used random forest machine learning (ML) models to predict receipt of seven distinct LSI categories from chief complaint words. Models were temporally validated in a separate cohort (CY2024; n = 9,838,357). Models demonstrated good-to-excellent performance for six LSI categories (AUROCs ranged from 0.929 for thoracic interventions to 0.821 for cardiovascular interventions). Model performance was consistent across training and validation cohorts, indicating temporal robustness. These findings suggest that AI approaches relying on natural language data could support timely, informed out-of-hospital emergency care.

title: Transparent chest radiograph foundation model enables explainable human disease profiling
abstract: Chest radiography (CXR) is widely accessible, and its ability to capture subtle manifestations of systemic disease remains underexplored. We developed a contrastively pretrained multimodal CXR foundation model using large-scale image-report pairs and evaluated its capacity to predict diverse human diseases. Using 1074 phecodes derived from electronic health records, we trained linear probes on frozen image embeddings and validated performance across three independent cohorts (n = 90,911; n = 79,786; n = 60,282). The model significantly predicted 554 prevalent and 457 incident phenotypes, with 60 prevalent and 42 incident phenotypes demonstrating consistently high discrimination across all datasets. To enhance interpretability, both diseases and 57 radiologist-curated CXR features were embedded into a shared representation space. This co-embedding analysis identified 28 phenotype clusters driven by recognizable imaging patterns, including cardiomegaly, atherosclerosis, and ground-glass opacities, and enabled reconstruction of most predictions with strong explanatory performance (R² ≥ 0.85). Importantly, the embeddings captured imaging signatures associated with near-term cardiovascular events and critical illness. These findings demonstrate that CXR foundation model embeddings encode rich, clinically relevant information beyond conventional interpretation, providing a scalable and interpretable framework for comprehensive disease profiling and a foundation for future prospective validation.

title: mnorm: An R Package for Calculation and Differentiation of Conditional Multivariate Normal Densities and Probabilities
abstract: We introduce the mnorm package, which allows one to calculate conditional multivariate normal densities and probabilities and to differentiate them with respect to various parameters including covariances and integration limits. The package also supports parallel (multi-core) computing, handles non-normal marginals via the Gaussian copula, and provides fast routines for the calculation of bivariate and trivariate normal probabilities. The package is of special interest for the implementation of the maximum-likelihood estimators in econometric models.

title: Evaluating covariate balance for long time horizon Markov decision processes
abstract: This article explores the application of covariate balance diagnostics for detecting the presence of hidden confounding/model miss-specification in studies applying offline reinforcement learning (RL) to deriving optimal treatment recommendations. The results demonstrate that, either there is a high risk of bias within existing offline RL studies for treatment recommendations and/or, existing covariate balance metrics are not sufficient to assess such studies. Regardless, existing offline RL studies cannot be concluded as being statistically robust. The conclusions propose future research directions for obtaining more methodologically robust applications of offline RL to treatment recommendation problems.

title: WorkDrive: Roadwork Chain of Causation for Autonomous Driving
abstract: Autonomous driving vision-language models (VLMs) struggle in roadwork zones, where familiar visual cues such as lane markings and permanent signs are altered or absent, and temporary devices such as cones and barriers redefine the drivable corridor. VLMs can detect these objects, but without explicit guidance they anchor their reasoning on familiar elements from pre-training and fail to connect work-zone observations to correct planning decisions. We propose WorkDrive, a framework that constructs perception-grounded causal reasoning for work zones and aligns it with trajectory prediction. An automated multitask perception pipeline extracts structured scene facts and injects them into a Chain-of-Causation (CoC) annotation pipeline, redirecting the annotator's attention to domain-specific elements. The resulting reasoning labels are used for supervised fine-tuning, followed by reinforcement learning with a single reward: consistency between lateral meta-actions and the predicted trajectory. On ROADWork, the largest public work-zone dataset, the proposed roadwork CoC reduces trajectory average displacement error (ADE) by 9.0\%, and consistency-based GRPO yields a further 3.0\%, achieving progressive improvement over the trajectory-only baseline. Code and data will be publicly released.

title: Class Weighting versus Amount Conditioning in Credit-Card Fraud Detection: A Dollar-Metric Study with a Temporal Explanation Audit
abstract: Credit-card fraud losses are monetary, but papers often judge models with transaction-level scores. We ask whether transaction amount should shape training weights or be used later to order alerts. To separate this question from ordinary class imbalance handling, we keep total fraud-case weight fixed and vary only its allocation across fraud cases. The experiments test two chronological card-fraud datasets with XGBoost under unweighted training, standard class weighting, matched log-amount weighting, stronger amount-weighted variants, and score times amount reranking. Metrics are average precision, dollar recall, and dollar precision at fixed alert budgets over five seeds, with 95 percent day-block bootstrap intervals for the main contrasts. Results are narrower than expected. Amount-derived ratio and velocity features carry much of the signal, while raw amount fields add little once those features are in the model. In the matched setting, amount-conditioned training gives only small gains over class weighting and does not consistently beat the plain unweighted model. Stronger amount weights recover more fraudulent dollars, but at lower ranking quality and dollar precision. Reranking alerts by score times amount after training gives the largest dollar-recall shift. A small SHAP audit finds larger month-to-month attribution movement for fraud cases than for aggregate traffic. In these tests, amount is useful as a feature and as an alert-ordering variable, not by itself as a better sample-weighting rule.

title: Verification code and pre-registration record — FP-292 to FP-320: the transcribed loop, the forced-light editor, the light-tax scaling, the replication battery, the real-model forced-light edit, the verb-edit wall and its fall, the lock-versus-audit experiments, the seed battery, and the five-verb table
abstract: Complete verification bundle for experiments FP-292 through FP-320 of the research program(companion to deposits 0..0j and the paper "The Forced-Light Editor: AuditableSelf-Modification in Language Models — An Existence Result, the Price of the Light, and theFall of the Wall"): every run script, results JSON, and run log present in the programrepository at assembly, plus provenance documents listing every pre-registration seal andbank commit hash (each seal committed to git BEFORE the experiment was built) and verbatimledger excerpts (blocks 4o80..4o9a for the original arc; 4oan..4obd for the extension). The ORIGINAL ARC (FP-292..299) is as in the superseded 35-file bundle: the transcribed loop(auditable latent reasoning in a from-scratch looped transformer, with the run-1 void and thecapacity-limited retry shipped); the forced-light editor toy (LIGHT-IS-CHEAP: the taught,fully-audited editor pays ~zero capability tax; THE GRADIENT PREFERS THE DARK: a provablyrate-matched readable channel that task loss alone never finds); the light-tax scaling (thecost is learnability, never capability; a starved channel collapses exactly to theinformation ceiling); the three-seed replication battery; the real-model forced-light edit(pythia-410m content edits at tax 0.000, log-closure 1.000, while the FREE edit lands ~64%readout-invisible); the original verb-edit wall (two sealed tries); emergence pressure(zero-label consistency mode-collapses; sparse supervision buys the readable code); and thetax curve (the taught editor rides the Bayes ceiling at every channel width). The EXTENSION (FP-313..FP-320) is the resolution and hardening of that wall, shipped withits voids and errata: FP-314/315 (two further edit instruments that walled — multi-layertied edits cannot fit; context-varied training memorizes noun identity); FP-316 (the premisecheck that re-diagnosed the wall as partly a TASK-SELECTION error: bare-token pluralizationis a computation the model never performs); FP-316B (routing a real verb generalizes 0.70;the projected-lit collapse later refuted as a projection artifact); FP-316C/D (TRAINEDlight-confined computation edits generalize at 1.000/0.90 with tax +0.000 — auditablecomputation editing exists); FP-316E (the law holds across pythia-1.4b/2.8b andQwen2.5-7B-Instruct at best-layer tax +0.000, with a universal depth texture: the dark editdegrades deep in the stack while the lit edit holds); FP-318/318B/318C (lock-versus-audit:across six lock constructions on two behaviors only two ever engage, both are routed aroundat 1.000, and both route-arounds are legible to a light monitor — including the bankedERRATUM 4oay-R that the first "engages at k=64" claim was a silent rank-40 truncation,caught by an adversarial pre-run review before any new run); FP-319 (the seed battery:six cells, every one dark 1.000 / lit 1.000 / tax +0.000); FP-320 (the five-verb table:comparative, third-person, and the SEMANTIC antonym map confine — two of the five verbsrequiring few-shot carriers after their bare carriers failed the premise check); and FP-313(a void rig, shipped as the record requires). Nulls, voids, sealed-prior misses, and errataare shipped deliberately: the record is the method. All identifying infrastructure detailsare redacted with the series' token conventions; hardware-class labels are retained whereload-bearing. title: XLM-R Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer via Multilingual Intermediate Tasks
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the impact of using intermediate tasks from multiple languages (not just English) on the zero-shot cross-lingual transfer performance of XLM-R on the XTREME benchmark? title: Adaptive Inquiry-Based Learning Applications for Enhancing Students' Critical Thinking Skills: An Innovative Approach
abstract: Despite the urgency of fostering critical thinking in the Society 5.0 era, conventional digital learning often overlooks individual learner diversity, particularly in the post-pandemic educational landscape. This study addresses this gap by developing and validating a cloud-hosted learning application based on the Adaptive Inquiry Approach. Utilizing a Research and Development (R&D) methodology via the six-stage Luther-Sutopo model (concept, design, material collection, assembly, testing, and distribution), the platform dynamically tailored multi-modal content (text, audio, video, and simulations) to match diverse learning styles (visual, auditory, read/write, and kinesthetic) for elementary students (grades IV–VI). The findings indicated that validation by an interdisciplinary panel of experts established outstanding conceptual, pedagogical, and technical viability, with all composite evaluation scores exceeding the 80% threshold. Concurrently, empirical assessment instruments demonstrated optimal item difficulty and robust discriminatory power in tracing cognitive gains, while supplementary guidebooks achieved high institutional feasibility. By shifting from a static, uniform instructional delivery model to a dynamic, algorithmically tailored inquiry framework, this platform bridges the digital-pedagogical divide without diluting instructional substance. This study contributes to the educational technology literature by offering a powerful, scalable blueprint to systematically empower students' critical thinking skills in the post-pandemic era.

title: Quantum kernel-based delta (Δ)-learning for correcting a semiempirical method in the prediction of reaction barrier heights
abstract: A quantum machine learning based Δ-learning framework is presented for the prediction of reaction barrier heights of organic molecules. Corrections learned by quantum kernel-based models are applied to mitigate the underlying errors of the semiempirical PM7 method, improving its predictive accuracy toward results obtained at the ωB97X-D3/def2-TZVP level of theory. Both fidelity and projected quantum kernels are implemented using seven distinct encoding circuits and passed to three classical regression algorithms, namely, support vector regression, kernel ridge regression, and Gaussian process regression, yielding a total of 840 benchmarked model configurations across circuit widths of up to 9 qubits and circuit depths of up to five layer repetitions. The encoding circuits are additionally characterized in terms of their expressibility and entangling capability. The top-performing models, constructed using the 9-qubit YZ-CX encoding circuit, predict reaction barrier heights with a mean absolute error ranging between 4.95 and 5.03 kcal/mol, underscoring an improvement of ∼54% over the uncorrected PM7 baseline.

title: Knowledge structure and future directions in emotional AI tourism research
abstract: Abstract The rapid integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in tourism services has accelerated the development of emotionally responsive technologies, yet research on Emotional Artificial Intelligence (EAI) remains fragmented across multiple domains and lacks a coherent framework explaining how emotionally adaptive technologies shape tourism experiences. This study addresses this gap by mapping the intellectual structure, thematic evolution, and future directions of EAI research in tourism. Using a systematic literature review combined with bibliometric and science-mapping techniques, the study identifies dominant research themes, influential knowledge domains, and emerging research frontiers. The findings reveal a clear conceptual progression from affective computing and emotion recognition toward emotional intelligence, human–AI interaction, emotionally adaptive AI, and human–AI co-creation. The thematic evidence further highlights growing attention to ethical governance, workforce adaptation, and traveler well-being as integral dimensions of EAI-enabled tourism services. Grounded in these thematic patterns, the study proposes the Human–AI Co-Creation Servicescape (HACS) framework, which integrates Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory and the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework to provide a multilevel conceptual explanation of how technological drivers, psychological processes, governance conditions, and socio-technical infrastructure collectively shape tourism experiences and service outcomes. The study contributes to EAI scholarship by synthesizing fragmented research streams into a coherent conceptual structure and identifying promising directions for future research.

The thematic evidence further highlights growing attention to ethical governance, workforce adaptation, and traveler well-being as integral dimensions of EAI-enabled tourism services. Grounded in these thematic patterns, the study proposes the Human–AI Co-Creation Servicescape (HACS) framework, which integrates Socio-Technical Systems (STS) theory and the Stimulus–Organism–Response (SOR) framework to provide a multilevel conceptual explanation of how technological drivers, psychological processes, governance conditions, and socio-technical infrastructure collectively shape tourism experiences and service outcomes. The study contributes to EAI scholarship by synthesizing fragmented research streams into a coherent conceptual structure and identifying promising directions for future research.

title: EdgeFaaS: A Function-based Framework for Edge Computing
abstract: Edge computing brings unique challenges as the resources on the edge are highly diverse in capabilities and capacities, and highly distributed across many users and the physical world. Existing distributed computing frameworks cannot adequately handle this level of heterogeneity and distribution. This paper proposes EdgeFaaS, a novel function-based edge computing framework to enable edge applications to effectively utilize heterogeneous resources distributed across the Internet of Things (IoT), edge, and cloud for computing. It proposes function virtualization and storage virtualization to abstract distributed and heterogeneous physical resources and provides consistent virtual interfaces for deploying and executing functions and storing and accessing data. EdgeFaaS provides comprehensive support to diverse edge computing workflows, and at the same time allows users to flexibly adjust the configurations and explore various important tradeoffs. To demonstrate its usability, the paper also presents the implementation and evaluation of three representative workflows on EdgeFaaS for video analytics, federated learning, and audio classification, on a real testbed of 100+ geographically distributed IoT devices, edge servers, and cloud services. EdgeFaaS allows users to flexibly explore the deployment configurations of these workflows over distributed and heterogeneous resources. For example, users can easily vary the function placement of the video processing pipeline across IoT, edge, and cloud resources and study the tradeoff between computation and communication costs; users can also flexibly adjust the cluster count and size in the hierarchical federated learning system and explore the tradeoff between training accuracy and speed.

title: Fine-Tuning Methods for Robust and Private Small Language Models
abstract: The deployment of Artificial Intelligence within sovereign, single-tenant Document Management Systems is constrained by two interlocking requirements: sensitive data must never leave the organisation's infrastructure, and the underlying AI must run on the hardware already available within client environments, which rarely includes dedicated accelerators. The dominant enterprise paradigm - Retrieval-Augmented Generation paired with Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of medium-scale Large Language Models - does not satisfy these constraints in practice, leaving a methodological gap for organisations that need domain-specialised AI under genuine sovereignty. This dissertation investigates whether sub-1B-parameter Small Language Models, specialised through Full Fine-Tuning on carefully selected documents, can serve as a viable alternative for this setting. The comparison between full-parameter and parameter-efficient adaptation in this regime is treated as an open empirical question rather than a settled one, and two contributions are advanced in addressing it. The first is the Knowledge Graduation framework, which reframes the choice between retrieval and fine-tuning as a document-selection problem: stable, structurally dense documents are internalised into the model's parametric memory, while dynamic operational content is served through retrieval. The second is a controlled empirical comparison of Full Fine-Tuning against Parameter-Efficient baselines on a real enterprise corpus, which provides consistent evidence that full-parameter adaptation of sub-1B models attains higher domain fidelity than low-rank alternatives while remaining deployable on standard on-premise hardware. The work is realised as a reproducible, end-to-end sovereign pipeline integrated with the iPortalDoc Document Management System. On the evidence gathered - obtained entirely on commodity on-premise hardware and confined to a single technical domain, with the hybrid retrieval comparison and multi-domain extension identified as ongoing work - the small-model-with-full-fine-tuning trajectory emerges as a credible alternative to the medium-model-with-PEFT paradigm in resource-constrained enterprise environments

title: Banya AI 3: Orthogonal Data-Operation Tokens and Convolutional Scale-Depth Structure - Label-Free Emergence of Operation-as-Weight
abstract: We view language as an orthogonal product of data (content: what a thing resembles) and operation (transformation: how it changes things). In this view, a single token exists as an orthogonal pair of two embeddings, a data plane and an operation plane. We call this orthogonal-pair token a bi-token. Its defining feature is that which plane is data and which is operation is never labeled in advance - only geometry (orthogonality) and positional asymmetry (an additive slot versus a multiplicative slot) are enforced. The data plane is content added to the residual stream, and the operation plane is a multiplicative gate that opens and closes the channel valves of the next token. Without labeling which token is data and which is operation, enforcing only geometry and positional asymmetry makes the operation plane emerge as a consistent operator that acts in a consistent direction on any data. We measure this and show the following. The directional consistency of operators is 10.1 times that of random; 72.5 percent of distinct operations are orthogonal to each other; and turning the operation plane on lowers the cross-entropy of next-word prediction by 2.79 (from 2.99 to 0.20, over 200 windows of the bundled self-made elementary dialogue corpus). Token identities split to the data and operation extremes, and the middle is empty. Channel mixing uses a circulant filter bank instead of a dense matrix, forming a ladder of depth and scale in which shallow layers become broad brushes and deep layers fine pens. This sequential composition carries the syntagmatic relation (order) of language, and order is handled by the mixing heads. All 16 mixing heads look at the same distance at the start of training and, by the end of training, differentiate to divide up different distances from 39 to 66 positions in the past. Finally, we measure the assembly discrimination of stem-ending combinations never seen in training using minimal pairs. On 198 unseen combinations, accuracy is 86.9% under the reversal distractor and 87.7% under the ending-internal swap distractor, far above the 50% chance level, and it holds even while a syllable-bigram baseline collapses to 47.7% on the hard distractor. We make no causal claim that the orthogonal structure is the cause, as no control model is available. This record contains the English edition (_en.pdf) and the Korean original (_kr.pdf). Part 3 of the six-part Banya AI research series. Part 1: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21385447. Part 2: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21385516. All measured figures are reproducible with the public code package: https://ubmscoin.github.io/banya/banya_ai_paper_code/ (code Apache-2.0). Frozen model checkpoints: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21383724

title: Parameter Scaling and Intermediate-Task Transfer in XTREME-R Zero-Shot Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does increasing model scale from base to large parameters diminish the relative performance gain of English intermediate-task training for zero-shot transfer on the XCOPA and XNLI subsets of XTREME-R? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.3/10.

title: ON THE CYCLIC SYMBOL-PAIR AND b-SYMBOL DISTANCE OF THE TERNARY [11, 6, 5] GOLAY CODE
abstract: We give a self-contained cyclic-code derivation of the cyclic symbolpair and $b$-symbol distances of the ternary $[11,6,5]_3$ Golay code $\mathcal{G}_{11}$. The pair distance is $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{p}}\left(\mathcal{G}_{11}\right)=7$, and the $b$-symbol distance profile is $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{b}}\left(\mathcal{G}_{11}\right)=5,7,8,9,10$ for $b=1,2,3,4,5$ with $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{b}}\left(\mathcal{G}_{11}\right) =11=n$ for $6 \leq b \leq 11$ (and under the periodic window convention for all $b \geq 6$ ). The numerical profile for $b \leq 5$ agrees with the recent symbol-block hierarchy reported by Guan-Luo-Luo-Fei-Wang; the contribution here is a compact direct cyclic-support proof and a $\mathrm{run} /$ gap refinement for $\mathcal{G}_{11}$. In particular, the 66 distinct supports of the 132 weight- 5 codewords split into six cyclic support orbits, each giving two scalar-multiple ternary codeword orbits. Thus, the weight- 5 codewords split into 12 cyclic codeword orbits, with 4 orbits each at $r=2,3,4$ maximal cyclic nonzero-runs and none at $r \in\{1,5\}$.

title: A survey on chatbot systems from rule-based models to system-integrated natural user interfaces
abstract: Chatbot systems have evolved from rule-based conversational tools to advanced data-driven systems that support more complex interaction. This paper examines this evolution and examines how advanced chatbot systems may function as System-Integrated Conversational Natural User Interfaces (System-Integrated Conversational NUIs). In this role, natural-language interaction serves as a user-facing interface to broader digital capabilities rather than only supporting conversational response generation. The paper provides a structured review of key stages in chatbot development, introduces the System-Integrated Conversational NUI as an interface-centred concept, and proposes a conceptual architecture and design principles for this expanded interface role. Key challenges and future considerations are also discussed, with particular attention to interaction quality, system complexity, responsible operation, and the coexistence of conversational and structured interface elements. This study provides a conceptual basis for analysing and designing advanced chatbot systems that support natural-language access to connected digital capabilities.

title: Safe Execution of RL Policies Via Acceleration-Based CBF-QP Constraint Enforcement for Real-World Robotic Deployments
abstract: Reinforcement Learning (RL) has demonstrated remarkable capabilities for solving complex robotic control problems, but its lack of safety guarantees severely limits deployment on hardware. In particular, as legged robots and manipulators often operate near safety-critical boundaries, out-of-distribution states can lead to failure upon deployment. To address this, we introduce Acc-CBF-QP, an acceleration-based Quadratic Program (QP) safety filter using Control Barrier Functions (CBFs) that constrains any RL policy onto a safe set at runtime without modifying training. The method applies to unconstrained and Safe-RL policies, and enforces joint position, velocity, torque, and collision constraints within a unified optimization framework. A key contribution is the formulation of RL+QP tasks that regulate deviation from the RL command when constraints would otherwise be violated. We introduce a TorqueTask, minimizing torque deviation, and a Forward Dynamics Task, minimizing induced acceleration deviation, thus providing principled control over safety-performance trade-offs. Experiments on a 7-DoF Kinova Gen3 manipulator and a 19-DoF Unitree H1 humanoid, both in simulation and on hardware, highlight substantial reductions in constraint violations. On the real H1 hardware, a Safe-RL policy alone yielded 10.04 violations/s, which were reduced by 92% to 0.80 violations/s when augmented with Acc-CBF-QP. On the Kinova Gen3, Acc-CBF-QP fully eliminated violations. Nominal task performance of the RL objective is preserved in violation-free regimes. Under aggressive velocity commands on H1, Acc-CBF-QP improves execution by preventing constraint-induced shutdowns, yielding longer survival times. The full pipeline is open-source.

title: Full-data accuracy with fewer labels for training and fine-tuning machine-learning force fields
abstract: Machine-learning force fields (MLFFs) are reliable only near their training distribution, making efficient construction of diverse training sets a major bottleneck for both train-from-scratch and foundation fine-tuning workflows. Active learning can reduce this cost, but standard model-committee uncertainty is impractical for foundation MLFFs because each committee member requires a separate fine-tuning run. We present an active-learning workflow based on last-layer-projection regression (LLPR), a forward-pass-cheap per-configuration uncertainty estimator. Across molecular, condensed-phase, and electrolyte systems, LLPR identifies compact, high-value training sets that recover full-data accuracy using only a small fraction of electronic-structure labels. In foundation-model fine-tuning, LLPR-selected configurations reach the full-pool fine-tuning ceiling with substantially fewer labels than random selection. In iterative electrolyte fine-tuning, LLPR detects unphysical local coordination before DFT labelling, provides an absolute force-error threshold, and enables automatic termination of the learning loop. The resulting models reproduce reference density and ion-coordination structure, providing a scalable uncertainty-quantification strategy across MLFF training regimes.

title: Engineering's Next Great Transformation: Why Organizational Capability Will Define the AI Era
abstract: Engineering has never had more computing power. Yet engineering transformation has never been more difficult. Over the past four decades, engineering organizations have consistently responded to increasing complexity by investing in better technology. Faster processors. Larger HPC systems. Cloud computing. Artificial Intelligence. Digital Twins. Engineering data platforms. Agentic AI. And now Quantum Computing. Each generation of technology has expanded what engineers can achieve. Today’s engineering teams possess computational capabilities that previous generations could scarcely imagine. Yet a remarkable paradox has emerged. While technology has advanced at an extraordinary pace, many organizations continue to struggle with turning technological progress into everyday engineering practice. The next bottleneck is no longer primarily technology. It is organizational capability. And that may become the defining engineering challenge of the AI era.

Contents: FP-310, the capacity knee (working state is slot-bounded at n*=4 while the summedcontent is conserved to n=64 — about two reliably deliverable items; the knee inverts to theread's effective dimension, D_eff ≈ 11); FP-310R, the second seed lineage (knee 6, D_eff ≈14.3); the full-amplitude discriminator (the break is genuine cross-talk, not amplitudestarvation); FP-310B, the Qwen port that tripped the pre-registered out-of-distributionfence (shipped as the VOID it is); FP-311/311B, the scale ladder (the gated run's fencesfired and are shipped; the delivery re-score shows the ~2-slot ceiling unbroken from 410m to2.8b while the read superlinearizes with scale); FP-310C, the gentle injection (alpha-blendedwrites with a stage-0 dose calibration: gentle windows exist at the single-cargo level onboth Qwen2.5-7B and pythia-1b, but off-distribution collateral grows with n at fixed dose,so no dose survives the full ladder — the cross-family sub-line is closed asinstrument-bounded, with the dose-response mapped); and FP-321, reader versus medium (try 1voided on its own mismatched-item falsifier and ships as such; try 2, with differentialtemplates, shows an optimal codebook-equipped external reader breaks at n=4 against thenative n=6 — the capacity limit lives in the carried code, not the readout — and thereadable channel externally carries as much working state as the readout-invisible one).Nulls, voids, and sealed-prior misses are shipped deliberately: the record is the method.All identifying infrastructure details are redacted with the series' token conventions;hardware-class labels are retained where load-bearing. title: From Memorization to Generalization: A Neural World Model for Do-calculus Reinforcement Learning
abstract: ─────────────────────────────────────────────────OVERVIEW───────────────────────────────────────────────── The original DoRL paper queried a tabular, count-based world model R̂(s,a) under a do(a') intervention to update Q-values for unchosen actions. This follow-up traces a complete diagnose-and-fix arc for what happens when R̂ is instead a small neural network: does the mechanism survive; does it generalize to never-seen states; if it appears to, is that actually caused by the counterfactual mechanism or merely by the presence of a neural network somewhere in the pipeline; and, once that turns out to matter, can the diagnosis be turned into a fix? Ten experiments (the ninth a confound check, the tenth an abduction test on a new tabular-onlyenvironment; neither is part of the main neural-generalization throughline), all reported asmean +/- std over 5 seeds with paired significance tests for the central claims, not pooledpoint estimates.The paper also includes a Reproducibility Statement (exact commands and seed ranges for everytable/figure; full code at github.com/robomotic/causalrl) and a Broader Impact Statement: 1. Drop-in validation (Phase A). NeuralWorldModel (a gradient-trained MLP on a bounded recency replay buffer) is swapped into all three of the original paper's environments with every other hyperparameter unchanged. DoRL's recovery-speed and spurious-correlation-immunity results survive the swap. 2. A genuine generalization test (Phase B). A new environment, ContextGeneralizationCorridorEnv, withholds half of a high-cardinality context variable's values entirely during training. Read in isolation, DoRL with a neural world model looks like a clean win: 75.6% +/- 3.3% branch accuracy on never-seen contexts, vs. 49.5% +/- 5.0% for tabular DoRL and a 45.2% +/- 5.3% standard-Q-learning floor (tabular DoRL's edge over standard QL: p=0.057, marginal). 3. The missing baseline. A controlled ablation — NeuralQLearningAgent, ordinary Q-learning with an identically-encoded neural Q-function but NO world model and NO counterfactual update at all — reaches 92.3% +/- 3.1% on the same novel contexts, 16.7 points HIGHER than full DoRL. Read in isolation, this says neural function approximation alone, not the counterfactual mechanism, explains the apparent generalization. 4. A hyperparameter sweep. A 24-point grid over the counterfactual channel's two governing parameters (gamma_cf, alpha) recovers part of the gap (84.2% best found) but not all of it, ruling out mistuned defaults and localizing the shortfall to an architectural cause: DoRL's own Q-values remain a plain lookup table even when its world model is neural. 5. The fix. NeuralDoRLAgent applies DoRL's exact update rule — unchanged formulas, only the representation of Q changes — to a neural Q-function instead of a table. It reaches 94.3% +/- 0.9% on novel contexts (a positive but not independently significant 2.1-point paired edge, p=0.221), and, more decisively, 90.3% +/- 2.0% training accuracy against the no-mechanism baseline's 74.4% +/- 10.2% (a paired +15.9-point margin significant at p=0.020) — appearing before the test phase even begins, because NeuralDoRLAgent's world model consumes both arms' revealed rewards every step while the no-CF baseline only ever trains on the action it took. 6. Extrapolation, not just interpolation. Every held-out context in experiment 2 sits at distance 1 from two seen training values — the easiest possible generalization test. A harder split (train on the low half of the context range, test on the entire held-out high half) confirms the structured encoder's benefit is not an artefact of dense interpolation: every neural agent still clears 70% novel-context accuracy where every tabular agent is stuck between 16% and 24%. The counterfactual mechanism's edge over the no-CF control also widens under this harder split (+13.9 points vs. +2.1 under interpolation), though that specific widening is reported as suggestive rather than confirmed (p=0.145, wide CI) given the no-CF control's high variance at only 5 seeds. 7. Is the structured encoder circular? The state encoder used throughout (a normalized scalar for context C, preserving its ordinal structure) was hand-designed for this environment. Substituting a plain nn.Embedding(K, 8) with no ordinal structure imposed — the generic no-prior-knowledge default — for both the no-CF agent and the fix costs 12-21 significant points of test-novel accuracy and triples to quadruples their variance (p=0.015 and p=0.001), confirming the structured encoder does real work. But — against prior expectation — the learned embedding does not collapse to chance either (71.5% and 82.2%, both comfortably above every tabular baseline): a never-visited context's embedding row receives no gradient and stays at random initialization (confirmed in a dedicated unit test), yet the downstream network still interpolates something based on proximity to other trained embedding vectors, producing real but far noisier generalization. 8. Is the fix's own training machinery load-bearing? Replay buffer capacity (150) and gradient steps per environment step (4) were fixed throughout without justification. A sweep for the fix agent shows test-novel accuracy is essentially flat across a 12x range of buffer capacity (50-600) — the headline 94.3% does not hinge on that choice — but is sensitive to gradient steps per update: at the sparsest setting tested (1 step), accuracy falls to 88.9%, below the no-CF baseline's 92.3% reference, meaning the "fix beats the no-CF baseline" claim requires enough gradient steps to hold. 9. Abduction, tested directly (tabular only). Every environment above draws each arm's reward noise independently, so Pearl's formal abduction step (infer the exogenous noise from the factual instance, carry it into the counterfactual prediction) could not have improved anything even if implemented. SharedNoiseCorridorEnv is a new minimal two-armed environment with a per-step latent shared across both arms' rewards, giving abduction something to recover. Applying the abduction rule exactly as originally sketched (full weight on the factual residual) is not a clean no-op when the shared component is absent — it is measurably WORSE than the population regression it replaces (MAE 0.578 vs. 0.410 against the realized counterfactual reward), because it injects the chosen arm's own independent noise into a prediction that noise does not inform. An MMSE-optimal shrinkage weight, computed from the environment's known noise parameters (an oracle quantity, not learned online), fixes this: it weakly dominates both the no-abduction and full-weight baselines at every noise level tested, matching no-abduction exactly when the shared component is absent and approaching full-weight abduction as it comes to dominate (up to a 65% MAE reduction relative to no-abduction at the highest noise level tested). ─────────────────────────────────────────────────KEY FINDINGS───────────────────────────────────────────────── 1. The do-calculus mechanism is not an artefact of exact tabular lookup: swapping in a neural world model preserves 2-3x faster recovery than standard Q-learning across all three original environments, with correct spurious-correlation resolution in every seed. 2. Tabular DoRL's Level-3 advantage is undertested at the boundary of its training distribution: on state-action pairs never visited during training, its branch accuracy (49.5%) is only marginally distinguishable from standard Q-learning (45.2%) at conventional significance (p=0.057), both near the 50% chance line. 3. A comparison that varies both a novel mechanism and representational capacity (tabular vs. neural) at once cannot safely credit or discredit the mechanism. DoRL with a neural world model clearly outperforms standard Q-learning and tabular DoRL on novel contexts (75.6%) — apparent confirmation. A plain neural Q-learning agent with no counterfactual mechanism at all outperforms it by 16.7 points (92.3%) — apparent refutation. Both readings are incomplete. 4. The counterfactual mechanism's contribution is real, once a tabular-Q bottleneck (identified via a hyperparameter sweep that narrowed but did not close the gap) is removed by making DoRL's own Q-function neural too: 94.3% test-novel accuracy, above the no-mechanism baseline, with a statistically significant 16-point training-accuracy margin (p=0.020) explained by using strictly more of the reward information the environment already reveals. This is a methodological lesson beyond this paper: a result that looks like a clean negative can be a positive result for a mechanism with a representational bottleneck removed, rather than a positive result for the mechanism being unnecessary. 5. This advantage is not an artefact of an easy interpolation split: under a genuine extrapolation test (training on the low half of a context range, testing on the entirely-unseen high half), every neural agent still clears 70% novel-context accuracy while every tabular-Q agent collapses to 16-24%. 6. The hand-designed structured encoder is not circular (a generic learned embedding performs significantly worse and far less reliably), but it is also not the only route to some generalization (the learned embedding still beats every tabular baseline substantially) — the encoder is necessary for strong, low-variance generalization specifically, not for generalization to exist at all. 7. title: Effect of English-Only Intermediate-Task Scaling on XTREME-R Benchmark Performance
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: What is the effect of English-only intermediate-task scaling on inference latency and throughput for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer on XTREME-R benchmarks relative to multilingual task sequences? Autonomous synthesis report generated by Assignee Research. Tribunal consensus score: 9.2/10.

title: Effects of applying Gaussianising transformations to DNN embeddings before calculating likelihood ratios
abstract: This paper investigates the effects of applying multiple different sequences of transformations that aim to Gaussianise the distribution of deep-neural-network embeddings (DNN embeddings) before those DNN embeddings are used to calculate likelihood ratios using a model that assumes Gaussian distributions (Probabilistic Linear Discriminant Analysis, PLDA). The transformations were originally developed for non-forensic applications of automatic speaker recognition. This paper investigates the effects of applying the transformations under three different sets of forensically realistic conditions. The paper assesses the effects of the transformations with respect to theoretical properties of high-dimensional Gaussian distributions, and with respect to their impact on the performance of a forensic-voice-comparison system. Considering both the distribution and the performance criteria, the sequence of transformations that appeared to give the best results was: linear discriminant functions + centring + whitening + radial Gaussianisation. The results are potentially generalisable and not just specific to forensic voice comparison, i.e., they are also potentially applicable to use of DNN embedding to calculate likelihood ratios in other branches of forensic science such as forensic comparison of facial images.

title: Prediction-Only Distillation in Linear and Logistic Regression
abstract: Self-distillation (SD) is typically studied when the student is retrained on the teacher's original training inputs. In many practical deployments, however, the labeled training data are no longer available, and one has access only to the trained predictor and fresh unlabeled covariates. We study SD in this prediction-only regime through a fresh-X prediction-mixed scheme: a pure-distilled student is trained on fresh covariates pseudo-labeled by the teacher, and the final predictor is an affine combination of the teacher and student predictions. For ridge regression under proportional asymptotics, we derive deterministic equivalents for the optimally mixed prediction risk under general anisotropic covariance and deterministic signal. We show that this risk is strictly smaller than the teacher risk for almost every pair of teacher and student regularization levels, including when the fresh covariates are out-of-distribution and even when their covariance is isotropic. We further show that the optimal mixing weight cannot be identified from unlabeled data alone, but can be consistently estimated in a single post-training step using a small independent labeled calibration set, without additional model fitting. Finally, for binary logistic regression, we show that prediction mixing can outperform both the teacher and the pure-distilled classifier.

title: ESAR: Event-Based Synthetic Aperture Reconstruction
abstract: Event cameras report asynchronous polarity events when changes in log--radiance exceed a fixed contrast threshold, producing signed temporal contrast measurements rather than conventional image frames. We formulate monocular event-based imaging as a synthetic-aperture inverse problem for a static ground-domain log--radiance field $θ\in \mathbb{R}^{N_g}$. Instead of reconstructing a latent pixel-time volume $v \in \mathbb{R}^{N_pN_t}$, we impose the geometric relation $v=Pθ$, where $P$ maps the fixed scene into motion-dependent latent views. Aggregating events over finite time intervals gives the linearized model \[ APθ= b+η, \] where $A$ is a temporal differencing operator, $b$ contains signed binned event counts, and $η$ represents measurement and modeling errors. This decomposition exposes a synthetic-aperture structure: under near-nadir motion, successive projections are approximately shifted views of a common scene, while the composite operator $AP$ remains ill-conditioned because it combines spatial averaging with temporal differencing. We therefore use regularized inversion to recover $θ$. Numerical experiments on simulated data and real near-nadir Falcon Neuro event data show that the proposed $θ$-based formulation recovers coherent large-scale spatial structure, relative to dynamic latent-image and learned event-reconstruction baselines, while suppressing fine-scale texture.

title: Binary Gauss Stabilizers for Abelian Lattice Gauge Theories
abstract: Gauge theories and quantum error-correcting codes share the same underlying structure: both use constraints to identify a specific subspace of the full Hilbert space. In quantum error correction, these constraints are known as stabilizers, while in gauge theories they correspond to Gauss law. In this work, we consider a family of discrete Abelian lattice gauge theories described by a $\mathbb{Z}_{N}$ gauge group with $N$ an arbitrary power of two. In this setting, we find a set of stabilizers for the gauge-invariant subspace which is an alternative to the Gauss operators, and we call them binary Gauss stabilizers. We use this alternative stabilizer group to build practical error-correcting codes exploiting the gauge symmetries of the system without the addition of extra qubits. The applications of our finding are not limited to error correction though. We also provide a new strategy of gauge fixing to remove the redundancies based on our alternative stabilizer, which might provide advantages with respect to already-existing approaches such as the axial gauge. Our results provide new tools to study lattice gauge theories and their quantum simulation, and opens directions for future work at the interface of lattice gauge theory and quantum information.

title: Causal-Adversarial Probing of Clinical Covariates for Prostate MRI Grading
abstract: Deep learning models for prostate MRI-based cancer grading may encode clinical covariates that either reflect useful disease-related signal or non-generalising shortcut information, but their role is usually assumed. We propose a causal-reasoning framework for probing covariate dependence in MRI-based International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) Grade Group prediction. Rather than treating mpMRI as a direct cause of grade, we model MRI appearance and ISUP grade as observations of latent tumour pathology, and test whether candidate clinical variables act as nuisance correlates, disease-related proxies, or irrelevant covariates in the learned representation. We implement this using an adversarial framework that suppresses the decodability of individual clinical covariate at a time while preserving MRI-based grade prediction. The approach is developed and evaluated on 2,903 prostate MRI examinations, with external validation on 576 patients. We report a set of interesting and previously under-explored imaging-to-clinical-variable interactions in the context of deep learning generalisation. For examples, in binary ISUP Grade Group $\geq2$ classification, suppressing age, BMI, and alcohol use improved AUC by 1.23%, 0.84%, and 1.42%, respectively (all p < 0.05), suggesting reduced non-generalising covariate information; In contrast, suppressing PSA and prostate volume degraded AUC by 1.91% and 7.61% (all p < 0.001), indicating that these variables carried task-relevant signal. These findings show that adversarial covariate suppression can provide a practical representation-level analysis for distinguishing potentially harmful dependence from informative signal in prostate MRI grading models.

title: Implementación de sistema RAG para PDFs almacenados en repositorios CKAN: Creación de un Chatbot especializado en Guías Docentes de la UPM y un Dataset como Base Científica para probar su calidad
abstract: Actualmente, el acceso público a las guías docentes de la Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) presenta diversas limitaciones. Para dar respuesta a esta necesidad, se ha llevado a cabo el proyecto GUIA, que ha permitido a la universidad implementar un programa piloto para publicar dichas guías en repositorios de datos abiertos basados en CKAN, una tecnología ampliamente utilizada por instituciones públicas. Sin embargo, al publicarse en formatos estáticos (PDF), la recuperación de información específica sigue suponiendo un reto, obligando al alumno a realizar búsquedas manuales exhaustivas para localizar el documento deseado y extraer la información requerida. Es por esto que se ha desarrollado un asistente virtual (Chatbot) basado en la metodología RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) para automatizar y mejorar el acceso a esta información. El funcionamiento del proyecto se basa en un pipeline de ingesta de los documentos mediante Triple Chunking (estructural, semántico y recursivo), que se almacenan en una base de datos vectorial (Elasticsearch) para interactuar con Modelos de Lenguaje (LLMs), que podrán variar entre modelos locales o conexiones mediante APIs a estos modelos. Todo el ecosistema del proyecto está orquestado y se despliega mediante Docker. Para probar la eficiencia del sistema, ante la ausencia de un conjunto de datos de referencia estándar (benchmark) capaz de evaluar los resultados obtenidos de este asistente, se procedió con la creación de un dataset de evaluación ad-hoc con parejas de preguntas y respuestas de referencia para medir el rendimiento del sistema. Se han usado métricas como BLEU, METEOR y ROUGE-L, ampliamente utilizadas en el dominio del NLP (Natural Language Processing). Este dataset podrá ser utilizado para evaluar futuras versiones o nuevos proyectos que implementen conceptos nuevos o mejoras. Los resultados extraídos del proceso de evaluación confirman que la aplicación de estrategias avanzadas de segmentación (Triple Chunking) y motores de búsqueda híbrida reduce notablemente las alucinaciones de los modelos generativos. De este modo, queda demostrada la viabilidad de la arquitectura propuesta como una solución correcta y confiable para la consulta de la documentación académica oficial. Este trabajo no aporta únicamente una herramienta funcional, sino que establece un marco de referencia reproducible que permitirá medir y perfeccionar futuros sistemas conversacionales dentro del ámbito universitario.

title: The Three-Layer Wall: Authorship-Bias Controls for Generative Agent-Based Simulations
abstract: Agent-based simulations built to explore soft-domain questions face a structural credibility problem: the author writes both the mechanism and the metric, so the simulation can "discover" precisely what its author assumed. This paper presents the three-layer wall — a hard partition of every quantity into fixed ontology, tunable hypotheses, and measured outcomes, with one-way information flow — and four operational controls that enforce it: placebo arms, observability separation with metamorphic audit tests, random-stream isolation for causal attribution, and narration–physics separation. The discipline is demonstrated in a cosmological agent-based case study implementing a layered metaphysics as executable mechanism, including an endogenous cultural-transmission loop in which agents generate, distort, and are behaviorally influenced by their own mythology. The controls caught three real authorship-bias defects during development. Two findings that survived the full battery are reported: living cultural memory exhibits a measurable fidelity half-life (94% under 60 years; 46% past 150), and narrative influence on behavior is nonlinear — saturating reach below a salience threshold produced no behavioral effect, while at full strength the same channel shifted cooperation, reduced violence, and raised terminal attainment despite negatively-valenced stories dominating the myth pool. Code and experiments are open-source at https://github.com/spranab/soulsim.

title: Performance Gains from Intermediate-Task Training in Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer with Large Multilingual Models
abstract: Intermediate-task training---fine-tuning a pretrained model on an intermediate task before fine-tuning again on the target task---often improves model performance substantially on language understanding tasks in monolingual English settings. We investigate whether English intermediate-task training is still helpful on non-English target tasks. Using nine intermediate language-understanding tasks, we evaluate intermediate-task transfer in a zero-shot cross-lingual setting on the XTREME benchmark. We see large improvements from intermediate training on the BUCC and Tatoeba sentence retrieval tas Research goal: Does the performance gain from intermediate-task training in zero-shot cross-lingual transfer persist when scaling to larger, state-of-the-art multilingual models (e.g., Bloom, mBART) on XTREME-R, measured by accuracy across typologically diverse languages? title: Quantum-infused deep learning for dual-task thyroid ultrasound diagnostics
abstract: Accurate classification of thyroid nodules is essential for early intervention and improved clinical outcomes; however, its diagnostic performance remains limited by inter-observer variability, limited data availability, and class imbalance in ultrasound imaging. Although existing deep learning models have demonstrated strong performance, they often struggle to capture both global semantic context and fine-grained structural details under limited data. This study introduces a hybrid quantum– classical deep learning framework that leverages quantum variational filtering in tandem with transfer learning via ViT-B16 and EfficientNet-B3 to enhance feature representation. A multi-stage preprocessing pipeline was designed to improve input diversity and class balance. The model jointly performs binary tumor classification and Thyroid Imaging Reporting and Data System (TI-RADS) level prediction, achieving 94.2% accuracy for benign-versus-malignant tumor classification and 91.8% macro-accuracy for TI-RADS prediction. The proposed approach demonstrates promising robustness and generalization in limited-data environments, highlighting the potential of integrating quantum encoding with classical deep learning architectures for medical image diagnostics.

title: A Dual-Track Specialist Feature Fusion and Meta-Learning Stacking Ensemble for Cervical Transformation Zone Classification in Colposcopy
abstract: Cervical cancer remains a major global public health challenge, and the accurate classification of cervical transformation zones (TZs) constitutes a critical step in early detection and clinical decision-making. However, distinguishing between Type 2 and Type 3 transformation zones remains particularly challenging due to their high morphological similarity and the inherent interobserver variability associated with colposcopic assessment. In this study, we propose a novel Dual-Track Specialist Feature Fusion and Meta-Learning Stacking Ensemble architecture for the automated classification of cervical transformation zones using the Intel & MobileODT Cervical Cancer Screening dataset. The proposed framework integrates a global feature extractor based on ResNet50 (Gatekeeper) with a visual specialist based on InceptionResNetV2, trained exclusively on the most diagnostically ambiguous cases (Type 2 and Type 3). The extracted features are fused and processed through a multi-level stacking scheme composed of Multilayer Perceptron (MLP), Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosting (GB), XGBoost, and LightGBM classifiers at the base level, followed by an XGBoost meta-learner and a clinically guided probability calibration strategy designed to maximize diagnostic sensitivity. Experimental results demonstrate a peak overall accuracy of 91.22%, substantially outperforming the baseline ResNet50 model (70%). Furthermore, the proposed system achieved Recall values of 0.90, 0.90, and 0.94 for Type 1, Type 2, and Type 3 transformation zones, respectively, highlighting its ability to accurately identify diagnostically challenging cases. Ablation studies, Grad-CAM visualizations, and external-image validation experiments confirm that the proposed architecture improves discrimination between ambiguous categories, learns clinically meaningful representations, and maintains strong generalization capability across heterogeneous scenarios. These findings demonstrate the potential of visual specialization and calibrated meta-learning strategies for the development of artificial intelligence-assisted colposcopic decision-support systems.

title: Translating object structures from English to Finnish
abstract: Learning Finnish object structures is one of the most challenging aspects in Finnish language. Finnish has three object cases, which are often termed as genitive, nominative and partitive. This division may apply to singular nouns, but it does not apply to plural nouns and particularly to personal pronouns. Therefore, the more correct naming is genitive-accusative, nominative-accusative, and partitive. Although singular nouns appear in genitive and nominative form, they are in fact variants of the accusative case. All object forms can be systematically handled using this division. This paper demonstrates the translation of various sentences structures with direct object from English to Finnish.

title: Slop in AI: The Hidden Challenge of Messy Data and Imprecise Models
abstract: In the gleaming halls of Silicon Valley and the bustling AI research labs around the world, there is often talk of elegant algorithms, lightning-fast processing, and the marvels of machine learning. But beneath this polished veneer lies a less glamorous reality that every AI practitioner must grapple with: slop. In the context of artificial intelligence, “slop” refers to the messiness, imprecision, and noise inherent in both data and models – factors that can significantly impact the performance and reliability of AI systems.\n

title: What is Artificial Intelligence?
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has evolved from a speculative concept into one of the most transformative forces shaping the 21st century. Once confined to science fiction and academic theory, AI now permeates daily life – from voice assistants and autonomous vehicles to AI-powered medical diagnostics and large language models like ChatGPT. This chapter provides a comprehensive overview of AI: its history, core concepts, subfields, applications, and the emerging ethical and societal questions surrounding its widespread adoption.

title: Performance Model for Hybrid Quantum-Classical Workflows
abstract: Hybrid quantum-classical workflows are expected to underpin practical quantum computing applications, yet the quantum and HPC communities lack a shared framework for reasoning about where and when their integration requirements matter most. Such a framework must separate two distinct levels of analysis: the application level, where communication overhead affects runtime performance, and the real-time level, where it determines feasibility. To address this, we introduce a runtime model that decomposes workflow execution into quantum compute, classical compute, and communication costs. At the application level, a communication-to-computation ratio from this decomposition quantifies whether a workflow is communication-bound or compute-bound; at the real-time level, a feasibility constraint determines whether timing requirements can be met at all, with the reaction time setting the logical clock speed of fault-tolerant computation once they are. Application of this model to representative workflows demonstrates that co-location of quantum processors with HPC infrastructure offers negligible performance benefit for compute-intensive applications today, while tight integration remains crucial for real-time tasks such as quantum error correction needed for large scale quantum computations. However, we discuss how even at the application level these assessments may shift with hardware evolution, illustrating how the model can identify specific crossover conditions, and how, under fault tolerance, the reaction time can set application-level performance.

title: Kernel weighted importance sampling for off-policy evaluation in contextual bandits
abstract: This article presents a novel estimator for performing off-policy evaluation using only offline data for contextual bandits. The proposed estimator, Kernel-WIS is demonstrated to be asymptotically consistent and to empirically outperform strong baselines (including weighted importance sampling), particularly under behaviour policy miss-specification. The benefit of Kernel-WIS is derived from combining the bounded property of weighted importance sampling with the linearity of vanilla importance sampling.

title: Immediate 3D Gaussian Splat Reconstruction of Unordered Input with Global Consistency
abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become the method of choice for reconstructing and real-time rendering of captured scenes. To capture a scene with good visual quality, continuous image sequences are usually combined with out-of-order shots for better scene coverage. Structure from motion can reconstruct such captures, but only after they are all available and often with high computational cost. Incremental reconstruction methods -- often derived from SLAM solutions -- provide immediate feedback, but cannot handle the out-of-order capture we require. We provide the first immediate feedback solution for such radiance field capture that provides global consistency. We first introduce a method for fast matching in out-of-order sequences, by repurposing visual place recognition models and a covisibility graph, and provide an efficient way to find highly connected keyframes, improving quality even for ordered sequences. We show how these steps -- together with GPU optimization and careful Gaussian primitive placement -- provide fast local reconstruction, in our challenging radiance field reconstruction case. We then introduce a novel cluster-based method, again using the covisibility graph, to provide efficient loop closure that does not require sequential input. Finally, to handle large scenes in our context, we introduce a progressive hierarchy that allows our method to scale to large environments, without compromising efficiency. Our results show we provide immediate feedback 3DGS reconstruction with good visual quality in several datasets, with up to thousands of input images.

title: Implementing Variational Quantum Algorithms to Compute Floquet Quasienergy Bands on Near-Term Hardware
abstract: Floquet engineering—the periodic driving of quantum systems—offers a powerful pathway to realize exotic nonequilibrium phases, including topological Floquet insulators and discrete time crystals. However, computing the quasienergy band structure of interacting, many-body Floquet systems remains a formidable challenge for classical computers due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space and the difficulty of diagonalizing the non-Hermitian effective Floquet Hamiltonian. In this work, we introduce and experimentally demonstrate a variational quantum algorithm (VQA) tailored specifically for the near-term computation of Floquet quasienergy bands. Unlike standard variational eigensolvers that minimize static energy expectations, our approach employs a parameterized quantum circuit to prepare variational trial states and directly extracts the quasienergy spectrum via a Hadamard-test-based cost function that measures the complex overlap with the single-period Floquet unitary propagator. By scanning the conserved crystal momentum, we reconstruct the full quasienergy dispersion for both one- and two-dimensional lattice models. We benchmark the algorithm against exact diagonalization for system sizes up to N=8N=8 qubits and subsequently deploy it on superconducting transmon processors, systematically characterizing the impact of decoherence, gate infidelity, and readout errors on the resolved band structure. To mitigate hardware noise, we integrate zero-noise extrapolation and measurement-error mitigation, recovering quasienergy features with fidelities exceeding 90% for shallow circuit depths. Our results establish that variational phase-estimation protocols offer a scalable, hardware-efficient route to exploring driven quantum matter, providing a practical toolkit for simulating Floquet topological phenomena on current-generation quantum devices well before the advent of fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: Future horizons
abstract: Owing to its large degree handling data in fundamentally novel manners, resulting in computational capabilities that were once unattainable, the interdisciplinary field of quantum computing has experienced a growth or increase in scope and garnered significant focus from the academic and business communities. Quantum computing holds significant potential; however, the precise manner in which it will revolutionize the future of healthcare continues to be predominantly uncertain. This chapter primarily focuses on the capacity of quantum computing to upgrade computationally demanding tasks in the medical field, interconnected in the realm of medical innovations, which encompasses pharmaceutical research, targeted therapy, genome sequencing, and next-generation sequencing. This report offers the fundamental interpretation of the various capabilities of quantum computing in propelling advancements in medical innovations. The dawn of a new age is driven by the integration of quantum computing and artificial intelligence (AI), which are set to revolutionize complex biological simulations, the analysis of genetic data, and progress in drug development. The vastness and complexity of biological data complicates the management of conventional computing tools, limiting the precision for medical advances. With AI&s;s predictive capabilities combined with quantum computers’ high processing speeds, biological analysis and clinical applications can be rapidly accelerated. This chapter focuses on the role of machine learning in fast-tracking of drug development through molecular mechanics, which can be grouped into AI-powered approaches that aim accept to replicate the action of particles with greater accuracy and efficiency, enabling the identification of potential drug candidates more quickly. By leveraging AI-driven simulations, scientists can explore complex molecular interactions, predict the efficiency of compounds, and optimize drug design processes. Quantum-enhanced algorithms facilitate quick modeling of chemical interactions, comprehensive analysis of drug-receptor binding strengths, and high precision in pharmaceutical kinetics. Additionally, we investigate quantum-assisted deep neural nets and artificial neural networks to improve forecasting disease advancement and pinpointing potential treatment targets. These models are directed to acknowledge complicated biological processes like protein folding, epigenetic alterations, and the connections between metabolic pathways.

title: Which CS1 Students Will Fail? Identifying Digital Markers from Learning Analytics in Computer Systems and Architecture Using Weighted Academic Momentum and Interaction Logs
abstract: Digital learning platforms generate rich behavioural traces (digital markers) that offer the potential to identify struggling students early. This paper investigates whether a combination of traditional and digital markers can predict failure in a first-year CS1 course (Computer Systems and Architecture) with sufficient recall to enable timely intervention. Using data from four cohorts (2017-2021, N=284) at a large public university in sub-Saharan Africa, we conducted a mixed-methods stakeholder elicitation to identify ten candidate factors. These were operationalised into a comprehensive feature set spanning demographics, self-reported surveys, Moodle interaction logs, and continuous assessment scores. A systematic ablation study using logistic regression with 5-fold cross-validation and SMOTE+ENN resampling revealed that the most predictive feature subset was Base + Demo + LMS: weighted academic momentum (M = 0.1Q1 + 0.15Q2 + 0.2Q3 + 0.55T1), basic demographics (gender, sponsorship, COVID-19 cohort), and a binary indicator of any LMS activity. On a held-out test set, logistic regression achieved 74.7% accuracy, 0.742 macro F1, and an AUC of 0.800. At the default threshold of 0.5, the model identified 87% of failing students (recall = 0.87) with a 41% false positive rate. SHAP analysis confirmed that weighted academic momentum is the strongest predictor, followed by its interaction with LMS engagement. These results demonstrate that simple digital markers can power a practical early-warning system by the fifth week of the semester. Our main contributions are: (1) a multi-source dataset and a stakeholder-guided methodology; (2) an ablation study quantifying feature group contributions; and (3) an interpretable, high-recall model ready for deployment.
